problem: 'Neither the universal machine nor the background matters beyond a constant factor' contradicts prop:basic:background, whose converse fails by an unbounded factor.
evidence: prop:basic:background last sentence; fundamentals Prop 4.3 and the sentence after it.
fix: Both propositions move to App A (BAS-L2 item 6); the main-text sentence is: 'The universal machine matters only up to a constant factor (\cref{prop:basic:invariance}), and building a background $B'$ into $B$ gains at most $K(B')+c$ bits on any data, while the converse fails (\cref{prop:basic:background}).'

problem: Cites a bound K_eq(T) <= K_A(D)+c of thm:basic:loss that the theorem does not contain.
fix: 'The bounds of \cref{thm:basic:loss} are stated with $\Keq(T)$, the length of a shortest index of a theory equivalent to $T$; for whole theories the question is how $\Keq$ compares with the mixture weight $\mmeq$.'

problem: Refers to a symbol e_{i,j} that the statement no longer uses.
fix: Delete the sentence 'Write $\zeta_{i,j}$ for the sentence $e_{i,j}$ of the statement, … (this avoids a clash with indices $e$).' (The statement itself moves to App A under BAS-L2; keep its notation.)

problem: Process 2 is said to be computable relative to the halting set, but its draws are infinite theories and its consistency test is Pi^0_1 relative to the tapes.
evidence: Definition of Process 2 in app-basic; fundamentals Prop 10.1(c).
fix: 'Process 1 is computable relative to $\emptyset'$, since consistency of a finite set is $\Pi^0_1$. Process 2 needs a consistency test relative to the tapes, which is $\Pi^0_1$ in them. Neither is computable, since a single draw of Process 2 can output one sentence.'
